newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania c.bank intervenes to bolster sagging lek.
newsitem.headline: Albania c.bank intervenes to bolster sagging lek.

text.p: Albania's lek currency gained some ground against the dollar on Wednesday after the central bank intervened to stop it plunging past its record low, central bank officials and traders said.
"We intervened today," a central bank official said, adding the currency then moved from 194 leks to the dollar to 189.
The official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the bank had sold dollars at 188.9 leks.
"This has stopped the mad devaluation of the last two days. It was speculation," the official added.

It was the lowest the lek has sunk since shady pyramid investment schemes collapsed earlier this year, sparking riots and political turmoil in the tiny Balkan state. The lek was valued at 104 to the dollar in January.
It fell on Tuesday from 175 to the dollar to 190, then slid to 194 on Wednesday before the central bank intervened. It later rebounded to 188-190.
Amid market uncertainty, some dealers were telling clients they could not even give them a price.
Traders had been seeking dollars for imports, while savers had continued to turn leks into hard currency, mainly dollars, fearing a further depreciation ahead of elections set for June 29.
Emigrants, whose remittances are a major source of hard currency, were sending home less money, "just enough for food", the trader said.
A commercial banker said depositors of two pyramid schemes, who were getting back part of their money frozen in state banks in January, were turning them immediately into dollars.
Increased interest rates on lek deposits had not had any effect on the market.
